SPLA/284/2024 (Application Seeking Leave to Appeal)

By this petition under Section 378(3) of CrPC, State/petitioner is seeking leave to appeal against the judgment/order dated 3.11.2023,
passed by First Additional Sessions Judge, Haldwani, District Nainital, thereby acquitting the respondent from the charges framed against them under Sections 376, 323, 506 IPC.
2.

entities.text: First Additional Sessions Judge, Haldwani, District Nainital
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Having heard learned State Counsel and on perusal of the impugned judgment and order,
following facts have emerged:
(i) Prosecutrix and accused, both are residents of Haldwani and they came into contact through social media some time in 2015.
(ii) Prosecutrix met the accused for the first time on 13.8.2015, when he proposed to marry her.
Prosecutrix was studying law at that time.

sentences.text: 1 (iii) Accused allegedly promised the prosecutrix to marry her and introduced her to his family members in December 2015 and his family members agreed to their marriage.
(iv) Accused respondent allegedly made false representation that he would marry her and made forceful sexual intercourse with prosecutrix in different hotels and other places at Haldwani.

(v) Accused respondent and the prosecutrix, both shifted to Dehradun in 2017 in connection with their studies and in Dehradun also, both used to meet each other in the room of the accused on every Saturday and Sunday, when the accused made forceful sexual intercourse with the prosecutrix, on the pretext of marrying her.
(vi) They last met at Dehradun on 26.10.2018 and the accused told that he would marry her in June 2019 and made sexual intercourse with her.
Thereafter the prosecutrix returned to Haldwani.
(vii) Accused respondent later disowned his promise, after she returned to Haldwani, and refused to marry her.
Prosecutrix admitted in her cross-examination that even thereafter on 13.6.2019, accused made forceful sexual intercourse with her.
(viii) Prosecutrix lodged the FIR on 29.8.2019.
(ix) In medical examination, no injury either on the body or on the private parts of prosecutrix was found and no opinion about rape was given.

(x) PW3 is the mother of prosecutrix and she, in her deposition, has stated that from 2015 to 2019,
the accused never came to her house nor she went to his house and, during this period, she made no effort for engagement of the accused and prosecutrix.
3.

In the backdrop of above facts and evidence, the Court below held that since the prosecutrix continued to have sexual relations with the accused respondent from 2015 to 2019 and her parents allegedly knew their relationship, however, during this period, parents of the prosecutrix neither met the accused nor his parents and also no effort was made to solemnize their marriage, therefore,
it cannot be said that the she gave her consent under misconception of fact i.e. on misrepresentation that the accused respondent would marry her.
4.
We find no reason to differ with the view taken by the Trial Court.

Prosecutrix was literate and intelligent enough to understand the significance, moral quality and consequences of the act she was consenting to and she admits it in her deposition, as noticed by the Trial Court, that the act she was indulging in was immoral.
Trial Court has rightly held that the allegations made by the prosecutrix cannot be construed as rape by the respondent.
Learned State Counsel could not point out any material/evidence, which the Trial Court failed to take account of.
